free_text: The patient is a 76-year-old male with a significantly elevated PSA of 13.6 ng/mL and a PI-RADS 5 lesion in the mid transition zone, corresponding to a confirmed ISUP grade group 1 carcinoma. The MRI shows a T1c clinical stage with no extracapsular extension. Given the low Gleason score and mild LUTS, the management assessment is active surveillance, balancing the potential benefit of intervention against the risks associated with treatment in this age group.
